plain_question: What do people pay for when they are buying time, relief, status, convenience, travel, attention, or escape?
social_or_cultural_insight: People spend to save time, repair mood, preserve identity, meet obligations, and feel alive inside a constrained schedule.
industrial_or_operating_insight: Service operators monetize repeatable capture of time, place, habit, attention, and convenience.
financial_or_investment_insight: Service revenue can reflect convenience and experience demand, but it can coexist with household stress and margin pressure.
representative_company_sets: lodging; restaurants; resorts/casinos; airlines; advertising; entertainment; staffing
proof_boundary: Service revenue does not automatically prove consumer health or durable discretionary demand.

plain_question: What does a household keep buying because it protects a routine, feeling, identity, habit, or sense of control?
social_or_cultural_insight: Households cut, switch, delay, and trade down while defending routines that make daily life feel manageable.
industrial_or_operating_insight: Consumer brands and packaging companies support routines, trust, shelf availability, and daily-use product flow.
financial_or_investment_insight: The strongest questions are repeat use, price/mix, private-label pressure, inventory discipline, and margin resilience.
representative_company_sets: personal products; beauty; packaged foods; beverages; apparel; toys; packaging
proof_boundary: Sales alone do not prove brand durability, pricing power, or cash quality.

plain_question: Which raw inputs become hard to get when many parts of the economy try to build at the same time?
social_or_cultural_insight: Material scarcity helps explain why ordinary life becomes more expensive even when final products look simple.
industrial_or_operating_insight: Power, housing, food, infrastructure, electronics, and industrial production depend on raw inputs and processing capacity.
financial_or_investment_insight: Materials companies matter when they control low-cost supply, scarce reserves, processing, logistics, or buildout-linked inputs.
representative_company_sets: copper; steel; fertilizer; chemicals; aggregates; lumber; uranium; aluminum
proof_boundary: End-market demand does not guarantee pricing power or high returns for every materials company.

plain_question: Who controls a place, site, lease, tower, store, medical location, or logistics node that someone else must use?
social_or_cultural_insight: Shelter, care, delivery, wireless coverage, travel, and compute depend on specific sites that cannot be instantly reproduced.
industrial_or_operating_insight: Location value appears through towers, data centers, logistics sites, medical facilities, lodging, housing, and retail nodes.
financial_or_investment_insight: The key questions are tenant need, lease duration, rent spreads, occupancy, debt maturity, and replacement cost.
representative_company_sets: specialty REITs; hotel REITs; retail REITs; healthcare REITs; residential REITs; industrial REITs; development companies
proof_boundary: Owning property does not by itself prove pricing power or cash durability.

plain_question: Which digital, hardware, network, or software control point must work before modern activity can continue?
social_or_cultural_insight: Digital life feels simple to users but depends on chips, networks, storage, software, identity, security, payments, and moderation.
industrial_or_operating_insight: Technology companies control work organization, compute, connectivity, data storage, cybersecurity, attention pricing, and digital interaction.
financial_or_investment_insight: The strong questions are control point ownership, recurrence, switching costs, AI cost exposure, retention, and cash conversion.
representative_company_sets: application software; communication equipment; IT services; semiconductor equipment; data storage; networking; telecom
proof_boundary: AI exposure, ARR, traffic, RPO, bookings, or user counts do not automatically prove durable value.

theme_family: Healthcare devices labs drugstores biotech and hospitals
plain_question: Which tools, tests, sites, distributors, and care systems make medical access physically possible?
social_or_cultural_insight: A patient can need care and still fail to receive it if tools, staff, sites, reimbursement, inventory, or authorization break down.
industrial_or_operating_insight: Healthcare access depends on devices, diagnostics, labs, drug distribution, hospitals, supplies, long-term care, and working capital.
financial_or_investment_insight: The key questions are procedure volume, installed base, consumables, reimbursement, distribution margins, receivables, payer mix, and regulatory risk.
representative_company_sets: devices; diagnostics; laboratories; drug distributors; drugstores; hospitals; biotech; long-term care
proof_boundary: More healthcare volume does not prove better outcomes, fair access, or better cash quality.

theme_family: Energy affordability upstream refining and service capacity
plain_question: Who controls the route from production to usable energy, and who absorbs the cost when that route becomes expensive?
social_or_cultural_insight: Energy affordability reaches daily life through commuting, food, rent, goods movement, utility bills, and industrial competitiveness.
industrial_or_operating_insight: Energy value depends on production, decline rates, refining, services, equipment, midstream routes, storage, and working-capital needs.
financial_or_investment_insight: The strong questions are realized prices, reinvestment needs, refining margins, utilization, hedges, balance sheets, and free cash flow after maintenance capital.
representative_company_sets: upstream oil/gas; refiners; marketers; oilfield services; equipment providers; midstream adjacency
proof_boundary: Volume growth, commodity strength, or high refining margin does not prove durable cash return.

theme_family: Ordinary finance banks cards brokers and insurance distribution
plain_question: How do deposits, card balances, insurance policies, brokerage accounts, payment rails, and loans change household and business behavior?
social_or_cultural_insight: Financial pressure reaches people through card balances, interest rates, deposits, premiums, lending standards, and payment costs.
industrial_or_operating_insight: Businesses depend on bank credit, deposits, payments, insurance, hedging, working capital, and transaction rails.
financial_or_investment_insight: The strong questions are credit quality, delinquencies, deposits, net interest income, fee durability, premium growth, losses, and retention.
representative_company_sets: money-center banks; regional banks; card lenders; insurance brokers; P&C insurers; exchanges; payment and credit services
proof_boundary: Scale in finance does not prove customer health, credit quality, or productive use of money.
